question: How many subscriptions currently have status active?
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS subscription_count FROM public.subscriptions WHERE status = 'active'

question: How many accounts are in each country? Return country and account count; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM public.accounts GROUP BY country

question: In how many distinct calendar months were paid invoices issued? Count months using invoice_date, considering only status paid.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date)) AS month_count FROM public.invoices WHERE status = 'paid'

question: How many high-priority support tickets are unresolved? Here unresolved means closed_at is NULL, including both open and pending tickets.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS ticket_count FROM public.support_tickets WHERE priority = 'high' AND closed_at IS NULL

question: For every plan with active subscriptions, return plan name and total active subscription seats. Exclude paused and cancelled subscriptions; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT p.plan_name, SUM(s.seats) AS active_seats FROM public.subscriptions s JOIN public.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE s.status = 'active' GROUP BY p.plan_id, p.plan_name

question: Which one plan generates the most current monthly recurring revenue (MRR) from active subscriptions? Return plan name and MRR in USD. Use the recurring-price metadata, not invoice payments. Break ties by plan name ascending, then plan_id ascending.
reference_sql: SELECT p.plan_name, SUM(s.seats * p.monthly_price_per_seat) AS mrr FROM public.subscriptions s JOIN public.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE s.status = 'active' GROUP BY p.plan_id, p.plan_name ORDER BY mrr DESC, p.plan_name ASC, p.plan_id ASC LIMIT 1

question: How many paid invoices were issued in each calendar month, using invoice_date? Return month (YYYY-MM) and paid invoice count; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(invoice_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month, COUNT(*) AS paid_invoice_count FROM public.invoices WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY TO_CHAR(invoice_date, 'YYYY-MM')

question: For each plan with paid invoices, what is the average paid invoice amount in USD, regardless of the subscription's current status? Return plan name and average amount rounded to two decimal places; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT p.plan_name, ROUND(AVG(i.amount), 2) AS average_paid_amount FROM public.invoices i JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = i.subscription_id JOIN public.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE i.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.plan_id, p.plan_name

question: For each support ticket priority with resolved tickets, return priority and average resolution duration in hours, rounded to two decimals. Measure closed_at minus opened_at; exclude tickets with NULL closed_at. No particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT priority, ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (closed_at - opened_at)) / 3600), 2) AS average_hours FROM public.support_tickets WHERE closed_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY priority

question: For each country with active subscriptions, return country and total active seats across its accounts. Exclude paused and cancelled subscriptions; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT a.country, SUM(s.seats) AS active_seats FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id WHERE s.status = 'active' GROUP BY a.country

question: Which five accounts generated the most paid invoice revenue in USD across all available history? Include paid invoices regardless of current subscription status. Return account name and total paid revenue, ordered by revenue descending; break ties by account name ascending, then account_id ascending.
reference_sql: SELECT a.account_name, SUM(i.amount) AS paid_revenue FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id JOIN public.invoices i ON i.subscription_id = s.subscription_id WHERE i.status = 'paid' GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC, a.account_name ASC, a.account_id ASC LIMIT 5

question: Which accounts have at least one currently active subscription but have never had a paid invoice on any of their subscriptions, including paused or cancelled ones? Return each account name once; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.account_name FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id WHERE s.status = 'active' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.subscriptions all_s JOIN public.invoices i ON i.subscription_id = all_s.subscription_id WHERE all_s.account_id = a.account_id AND i.status = 'paid')

question: Which accounts have subscriptions on more than one distinct plan? Include every subscription status and return account name and distinct plan count; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT a.account_name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.plan_id) AS plan_count FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.plan_id) > 1

question: For accounts in Japan, what is current monthly recurring revenue (MRR) in USD by plan tier, counting only active subscriptions? Return each tier with active subscriptions and its MRR using the recurring-price metadata, not invoice payments; no particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT p.plan_tier, SUM(s.seats * p.monthly_price_per_seat) AS mrr FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id JOIN public.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE a.country = 'Japan' AND s.status = 'active' GROUP BY p.plan_tier

question: Which accounts have more than 1,000,000 USD in total paid invoice revenue across all available history, regardless of current subscription status? Return account name and paid revenue; if none qualify, return no accounts. No particular row order is needed.
reference_sql: SELECT a.account_name, SUM(i.amount) AS paid_revenue FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.account_id JOIN public.invoices i ON i.subscription_id = s.subscription_id WHERE i.status = 'paid' GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name HAVING SUM(i.amount) > 1000000

question: Among accounts with at least one currently active Enterprise-tier subscription, which three opened the most support tickets? Count each ticket once across all ticket statuses, regardless of how many qualifying subscriptions the account has. Return account name and ticket count, ordered by ticket count descending; break ties by account name ascending, then account_id ascending. Include only accounts that opened tickets.
reference_sql: SELECT a.account_name, COUNT(t.ticket_id) AS ticket_count FROM public.accounts a JOIN public.support_tickets t ON t.account_id = a.account_id JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT s.account_id FROM public.subscriptions s JOIN public.plans p ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id WHERE s.status = 'active' AND p.plan_tier = 'Enterprise') eligible ON eligible.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id, a.account_name ORDER BY ticket_count DESC, a.account_name ASC, a.account_id ASC LIMIT 3
